# Judith Chapter 8 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 8

---

## Council Notes

**Key decisions for this chapter:**

**Judith's introduction (vv. 1-8):** All three translators handle her genealogy and biography straightforwardly. The key crux is v. 7 — her beauty. EMET: "very beautiful in appearance and comely-of-face." LOGOS: "very beautiful in appearance and exceedingly lovely to look upon." PNEUMA: "breathtakingly beautiful." SOPHIA: "very beautiful in appearance and exceedingly lovely to behold" — the double formulation (two Greek phrases) must be preserved.

**v. 11 — "is not right":** EMET: "is not right." LOGOS: "is not right." PNEUMA: "is wrong." All three converge. SOPHIA uses LOGOS: "is not right."

**v. 12 — "who are you, that you have tested God":** PNEUMA's "Who do you think you are?" captures the rhetorical force well. LOGOS is slightly more restrained. SOPHIA takes LOGOS's formulation as more appropriate to formal theological discourse.

**v. 16 — THE KEY VERSE:** EMET: "Do not pledge-as-security the purposes of the Lord our God." LOGOS: "Do not lay pledges against the purposes of the Lord our God." PNEUMA: "Do not try to bind the purposes of the Lord our God." This verse is the theological heart of the book. SOPHIA adopts PNEUMA's rendering — "bind" captures both the literal meaning (pledge/secure as collateral) and the deeper metaphor of attempting to constrain God's freedom. "Do not try to bind the purposes of the Lord our God" is the ruling.

**v. 27 — "as in a furnace":** The metaphor is obscure — the Greek suggests God's testing is like refining metal. EMET's "as they were in the furnace" is literal; LOGOS's "as if the fire were in their hearts" is paraphrase; PNEUMA's "send them into those fires" is loose. SOPHIA keeps the furnace metaphor but clarifies: "as he refined them in the furnace."

**vv. 33-34 — Judith's instructions:** All three translators handle Judith's deliberate vagueness correctly. SOPHIA preserves the secrecy emphasis.

---

**8:1** In those days Judith heard — Judith daughter of Merari son of Ox son of Joseph son of Oziel son of Elkiah son of Ananias son of Gideon son of Raphain son of Ahitub son of Elihu son of Eliab son of Nathanael son of Salamiel son of Sarasadai son of Israel.

**8:2** Her husband had been Manasseh, of her own tribe and family; he had died during the barley harvest.

**8:3** He was standing over the men binding sheaves in the field when the heat struck him on the head. They carried him to bed and he died in his city of Bethulia, and was buried with his ancestors in the field between Dothan and Balamon.

**8:4** Judith had been a widow in her house for three years and four months.

**8:5** She had set up a tent for herself on the roof of her house, put on sackcloth around her waist, and worn widow's clothing.

**8:6** She fasted every day of her widowhood, except the eves of the Sabbaths and the Sabbaths themselves, the eves of the new moons and the new moons, the festivals, and the days of rejoicing of the house of Israel.

**8:7** She was very beautiful in appearance and exceedingly lovely to behold. Her husband Manasseh had left her gold and silver, male servants and female servants, livestock and fields; and she had remained mistress over all these things.

**8:8** No one spoke an ill word about her, for she feared God exceedingly.

**8:9** She heard the harsh words the people were speaking against Uzziah their ruler, because they had lost heart over the lack of water; and she heard all that Uzziah had said to them — how he had sworn to hand over the city to the Assyrians after five days.

**8:10** She sent her maidservant, who oversaw all her affairs, to summon Uzziah and Chabris and Charmis, the elders of her city.

**8:11** When they came to her she said to them: "Hear me, rulers of the people of Bethulia! What you have said before the people today is not right — this oath you have sworn and pledged between God and yourselves, promising to hand over the city to our enemies unless within these days the Lord turns to help us.

**8:12** Who are you, that you have put God to the test today and have set yourselves in God's place among human beings?

**8:13** And now you are putting the Lord Almighty to the test — and you will never understand anything about him!

**8:14** For you cannot plumb the depths of the human heart or grasp the thoughts of the human mind. So how will you search out God, who made all these things — know his mind and comprehend his purposes? No, brothers — do not provoke the Lord our God to anger.

**8:15** For if he does not choose to help us within these five days, he has the power to protect us within whatever days he pleases — or equally, to destroy us before the face of our enemies.

**8:16** Do not try to bind the purposes of the Lord our God, for God is not like a man, to be coerced by threats, nor like a human being, to be won over by pleading.

**8:17** Therefore let us wait for the salvation that comes from him and call on him to help us. He will hear our voice, if it pleases him.

**8:18** For there has not arisen in our generation, nor does there exist today, any tribe or family or people or city among us that worships gods made by human hands, as was the case in former days —

**8:19** on account of which our ancestors were given over to the sword and to plunder and fell with great catastrophe before their enemies.

**8:20** But we know no other God but him, and so we hope that he will not despise us or any of our people.

**8:21** For if we are taken captive, all Judea will be taken captive and our sanctuaries will be plundered, and he will require their blood at our hands.

**8:22** The slaughter of our kindred, the captivity of the land, the desolation of our inheritance — he will bring all of this upon our heads among the nations wherever we are enslaved, and we will become an offense and a reproach before those who have enslaved us.

**8:23** For our slavery will bring no goodwill; the Lord our God will turn it to dishonor.

**8:24** And so, brothers, let us give our kindred proof — that their lives depend upon us, and that the sanctuary and the temple and the altar rest on our shoulders.

**8:25** Above all let us give thanks to the Lord our God, who is testing us just as he tested our ancestors.

**8:26** Remember what he did with Abraham, how he tested Isaac, and what became of Jacob in Syrian Mesopotamia while he tended the flocks of Laban his mother's brother.

**8:27** For as he did not destroy them when he refined them in the furnace, so he does not exact vengeance on us; rather his hand disciplines those who draw near to him, to admonish and shape them.

**8:28** Then Uzziah said to her: "All that you have said you have spoken from a good heart, and no one can find fault with your words.

**8:29** And this is not the first day your wisdom has been on display; from the beginning of your life all the people have known your understanding, for the disposition of your heart has always been good.

**8:30** But the people were in extreme thirst and they compelled us to do as we told them and to bind ourselves with an oath we cannot now transgress.

**8:31** So pray for us, for you are a devout woman — and the Lord will send rain to fill our cisterns, and we will be faint no longer."

**8:32** Judith said to them: "Hear me — and I will do a thing that will resound through every generation of our people.

**8:33** Stand at the gate tonight, and I will go out with my maidservant. And within the very days after which you said you would hand over the city to our enemies, the Lord will deliver Israel by my hand.

**8:34** But do not ask me what I am doing, for I will tell you nothing until the task is accomplished."

**8:35** Uzziah and the rulers said to her: "Go in peace — and may the Lord God go before you to take vengeance on our enemies."

**8:36** Then they turned from the tent and went to their posts.
